options: A way for each customer to run their own private copy of the Salesforce application on their own servers
A single shared application and infrastructure serving many customers, with each customer's data fully isolated from the others
A pricing model where customers pay based on how many buildings their company occupies
A feature that lets two different companies share and edit the same records
questions.explain: Multitenancy means every customer runs on the same shared application and servers, but data is walled off per organization so no tenant can see another tenant's records.

questions.q: Why can Salesforce push a platform upgrade to every customer at the same time, three times a year?
options: Because every customer manually downloads and installs the update themselves
Because Salesforce only has a small number of customers to update
Because every customer runs the same application code on shared infrastructure, so one upgrade applies to everyone at once
Because upgrades are optional and most customers skip them
questions.explain: Since all tenants share the same underlying application, a single platform-wide upgrade reaches every customer simultaneously — nobody schedules a separate install.

questions.q: What is a Salesforce 'instance' (also called a 'pod')?
options: A single user's personal login session
A dedicated server that only your company uses
A nickname for the Salesforce mobile app
The specific cluster of servers that physically hosts your org, alongside many other companies' orgs
questions.explain: An instance, or pod, is a specific server cluster (like NA123) that hosts many different companies' orgs at once.

questions.q: What are governor limits, and why do they exist?
options: Limits on how many employees a company can add as Salesforce users
Hard resource caps per transaction, which exist because shared infrastructure must be protected from any one tenant overusing it
A security feature that blocks unauthorized logins
Limits on how many Salesforce orgs one person can create
questions.explain: Because Salesforce is multitenant, it enforces governor limits — caps on things like queries per transaction — so no single tenant's process can degrade performance for everyone else sharing the same instance.

questions.q: Where can you check the real-time status of the specific instance your org runs on?
options: The Salesforce mobile app's settings menu
Your company's internal IT wiki only
There is no way to check instance status
trust.salesforce.com
questions.explain: Salesforce publishes real-time and historical status for every instance on trust.salesforce.com, which you'll work with directly in Lesson 15.
